instruction:
Differential-Pair Labelling

/home/user/Desktop/mipi.kicad_sch contains a MIPI D-PHY interface with 4 differential pairs drawn between an image sensor SoC (U1) and a 10-pin FFC connector (J1). The nets are currently named with arbitrary labels: D0A/D0B, D1P/D1N, CLK+/CLK-, D2plus/D2minus. A hidden property 'PadConvention' on J1 states the pad numbering rule.

Rename all 8 MIPI differential-pair net labels to follow the KiCad convention required for length-matching: <NAME>_P for the positive lane, <NAME>_N for the negative lane. The P/N assignment must be consistent with the connector footprint pad convention (even-numbered pad = P lane, odd-numbered pad = N lane). Use the standard MIPI D-PHY signal names.

Required net names:
- MIPI_D0_P / MIPI_D0_N (data lane 0)
- MIPI_D1_P / MIPI_D1_N (data lane 1)
- MIPI_D2_P / MIPI_D2_N (data lane 2)
- MIPI_CLK_P / MIPI_CLK_N (clock lane)

Requirements:
1. All 8 nets renamed exactly as listed above (uppercase _P and _N suffixes).
2. No original arbitrary net names remain as label text.
3. J1 Pad properties updated to reflect new net names.
4. U1 and J1 still present in the schematic.

Write /home/user/Desktop/mipi.kicad_sch.
source: MIPI D-PHY Specification v2.5, KiCad 9 Official Documentation — PCB Editor / Schematic Editor / CLI (diff-pair net naming `_P`/`_N`)
